title: A vendor credit for an internal work order's part posts where the bill did
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Approved, with one special-order part whose vendor bill of $125.00 posted to account X.
custom_steps:
1. Enter a vendor credit of $125.00 returning work order 1's special-order part.
  2. In QuickBooks Online, open that vendor credit.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The credit is saved.

Step 2:

  • The credit line posts to account X, where the bill line was posted.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R3a: “A vendor credit or a return for a special-order part or a core of an internal or no-charge work order posts its line to the account the matching bill line was posted to, and after Close to the work order's mapped expense account, so the credit lands where the cost did. A stock part returned to the shelf is a stock movement with no entry, as today.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
